in_arabic.name: جھان
in_arabic.long_meaning: جھان هو اسم مشتق من الجذر العربي 'ج-ه-ن' والذي يعني العالم أو الكون. في اللغة العربية، يُستخدم هذا الاسم للإشارة إلى كل شيء أو الكل. كما يمكن أن يعني العالم أو الكون كله. في السياق الإسلامي، يمكن أن يُستخدم هذا الاسم لوصف عظمة الله وخلقه للكون.

in_urdu.name: جہان
in_urdu.long_meaning: جہان ایک عربی मूल کا نام ہے جس کا مطلب ہے دنیا یا عالم۔ یہ نام اردو میں بھی استعمال ہوتا ہے اور اس کا مطلب ہوتا ہے کل شيء یا پورا کون۔ اسلامی تقليد میں، یہ نام خدا کی عظمت اور اس کے برخلاف کچھ بھی نہیں ہونے کی یاد دلاتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: जहान
in_hindi.long_meaning: जहान एक नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से आया है। इसका अर्थ है दुनिया, विश्व या सम्पूर्ण सृष्टि। यह नाम भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में भी प्रयोग होता है और इसका महत्व इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत अधिक है।

in_pashto.name: جهان
in_pashto.long_meaning: جهان د پښتو ژبې يو نوم دى چې ماناى يې دى نړۍ يا کائنات. دا نوم د پښتنو په مېشتو کې کارول کېږي او د افغانستان په اسلامي کلتور کې ځانګړى اهميت لري.

in_english.name: Jahaan
in_english.long_meaning: Jahaan is an Arabic-originated name meaning 'the world' or 'universe'. Derived from the root 'j-h-n', it signifies everything or the entirety of creation. In Islamic tradition, this name reflects the grandeur of God's creation and is often used to express the vastness of the world.

data.cultural_impact: The Islamic name "Jahaan" holds a significant cultural impact as it is derived from the Arabic word 'al-jahannam' which is synonymous with "the world" or "the universe". Historically, it has been used as a given name for both males and females in the Muslim world. In various contexts, it can represent the vastness and diversity of the entirety of creation, reminding us of the sheer magnitude and complexity of the universe and our place within it.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Jahaan" also holds deep spiritual significance in Islamic tradition. It is a reminder of Allah's infinite mercy and compassion towards His creation. In the Quran, Allah says, "He is the Irresistible, the Merciful. We have apportioned to each prophet friendship and loyalty. Some of them were on one another's right (in succession). Others were on the left (in turns). And others Allah guided from their mothers' wombs; and He made them grow up and cherished them. And He was the Guardian of them. And Allah is the Exalted in Might, the Wise." (Quran 35:24-26). This verse illustrates the intrinsic connection between us and the universe, as we are all part of Allah's creation, and the importance of cherishing and nurturing each other, just as a mother cherishes and nurtures her child. The name "Jahaan" serves as a constant reminder to live in harmony with not just those around us, but with the entire universe, and to recognize the interconnectedness and oneness of all creation.
